key_insight: RECONTEXT improves long-context reasoning by recursively replaying query-relevant evidence from the original context before generation, rather than pruning or retraining the model.
engineering_relevance: It offers a training-free, plug-and-play way to boost evidence utilization in long-context LLM applications without external memory or changes to model weights.
method: Use model-internal relevance signals to build a query-conditioned evidence pool.
Replay selected evidence before the final answer while keeping the full context intact.
Separate evidence organization from answer generation via a recursive selection loop.
evidence_signal: On eight long-context datasets with 128K context length, RECONTEXT improved evidence utilization across Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Llama3-8B, achieving the best average rank on all three backbones.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of internal relevance signals, so misselection could replay unhelpful evidence and add inference overhead.
paper_title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
